title: An end-to-end AI-based framework for automated discovery of rapid CEST/MT MRI acquisition protocols and molecular parameter quantification (AutoCEST)
summary: AutoCEST jointly optimizes CEST/MT acquisition schedules and a deep reconstruction network. Phantom measurements showed concentration error of 2.42 ± 2.53 mM (r=0.992), versus 65.19 ± 34.48 mM with an unoptimized schedule; mouse-brain imaging is a proof of concept, not clinical validation.
ai_technology: AutoCEST differentiable acquisition-schedule optimization and deep neural reconstruction
organization: Martinos Center, Massachusetts General Hospital and Harvard Medical School; Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics; University Hospital Erlangen

evidence.tested: Generated schedules took 35–71 seconds; phantom concentration maps closely matched known values and mouse-brain maps showed expected tissue patterns.
evidence.unknown: Validation is limited to chemical-exchange phantoms and one in-vivo mouse-brain setting; no clinical validation is reported.
evidence.ai_role: A differentiable system jointly optimizes CEST/MT acquisition schedules and a deep neural network for parameter reconstruction.

source_review.scope: Primary full-text Methods and Results and arXiv v1 reviewed; version chronology checked.
